title: A Cubic Separation Law for Wide Binaries: an Exponent With No Free Parameters
description: THE CLAIM, FIRST. In wide binaries wider than about 50 kAU the relative velocity should exceed the Newtonian value by an amount growing as the CUBE of the separation: gamma_v(s) - 1 = (1/2)[nu(y_ext) - 1] (omega_c^2/GM) s^3. The EXPONENT IS 3 -- derived, not fitted, and not tunable. Every known contamination channel in wide-binary samples rises as s^(1/2) instead. Exponent 3 against exponent 0.5 is the measurement. WHAT WOULD KILL IT: no excess beyond ~50 kAU in a contamination-controlled sample; a log-slope inconsistent with 3; a knee that does not move as M^(1/3); an amplitude inconsistent with omega_c^2/GM; or a boost gamma_v ~ 1.09 found INSIDE 30 kAU. WHERE IT COMES FROM. The framework is MODIFIED INERTIA -- the modification lives in the matter sector, not in gravity -- with a0 = cH_Lambda/Z = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32pi) = 9.36e-11 m/s^2, Z = sqrt(32pi/3) = 5.78881. CREDIT, PLAINLY: the interpolation nu(y) = sqrt(1+1/y) and the identity g_obs^2 - g_bar^2 = a0 g_bar ARE Milgrom (1999, Phys. Lett. A 253, 273) Eqs. (8)-(9) with coefficient 2cH_Lambda; Milgrom (1999, 2015) and Smolin (2017, PRD 96, 083523) had already tied a0 to Lambda with a 2pi coefficient. NO PRIORITY IS CLAIMED for the Lambda tie. What is ours is the coefficient cH_Lambda/Z, the modified-inertia completion, and this prediction. The second scale is a response gate K_eff = 1 - S(|a|/a0) G(omega), G = 1/(1+i omega/omega_c), omega_c in [1.782, 2.211]e-14 rad/s. WHY A GATE MUST EXIST, AND WHY ITS SCALE IS FREE. On the frequency axis |K| = 1 EXACTLY for every omega > a0/2c: the kernel saturates with no high-frequency roll-off, so it gives an inner-disk star and the Earth the SAME response. Since the solar system must be Newtonian and galaxies must not be, a frequency-dependent roll-off is REQUIRED -- the gate's existence is forced. Its SCALE is not: stated against interest, omega_c is a FREE PARAMETER. A dimensional census places every intrinsic scale of the theory 3.2-5.6 decades away, and consistency alone brackets it to only ~3 orders. So a0's value, Z, the sign s = -1, AND omega_c are postulated, not derived. THE BRANCH IS NOW SETTLED FROM THE ACTION (new in v2; v1 was explicitly conditional on it). The committed matter term S_matter = -(1/2) INT d^4x sqrt(-g) rho_m [s u^mu K(Box_u/a0^2) u_mu] has Box_u f = u^a nabla_a(u^b nabla_b f), the second derivative along the worldline. On a circular orbit u_mu is an eigenvector: Box_u u_mu = -Omega^2 u_mu IDENTICALLY (verified symbolically). So K's argument is the ORBITAL FREQUENCY, z = -(Omega c/a0)^2. The acceleration MAGNITUDE |a| = Omega^2 R genuinely is constant on a circular orbit, but the action never feeds |a| to K. Had it done so the gate would stay open and the prediction would be gamma_v ~ 1.09; it does not. THE GATE IS SHUT WHERE EVERYONE MEASURES. A 1.5 Msun pair at 10 kAU has Omega = 2.44e-13 rad/s, 11x above the TOP of the whole omega_c window; Re G = 0.005-0.008 and gamma_v = 1.0004-1.0006, within 0.04 sigma of Newton. Two radii run opposite ways: r_M = sqrt(GM/a0) (sub-a0 begins) and r_gate = (GM/omega_c^2)^(1/3) (gate opens). Since Omega ~ s^-3/2 while g ~ s^-2, always r_gate > r_M -- ratio 4.54-7.76 across 0.5-3.0 Msun, both footings, both edges -- so between them a pair is already sub-a0 but still gate-shut and must look NEWTONIAN. For 1.5 Msun that dead zone runs ~10 to ~50-60 kAU. GALAXIES ARE UNTOUCHED, which is what makes the gated reading admissible: across the MW solar circle and outer disk, dwarfs, LSB disks, massive spirals and the inner disk the largest Omega/omega_c is 0.364 (Re G >= 0.883), so the RAR and BTFR are unaffected. THE EXPONENT COUNTS POLES (new in v2). An n-pole gate gives |G_n|^2 -> (omega_c/Omega)^(2n), hence gamma_v - 1 ~ s^(3n) and n = p/3. Verified numerically at n = 1,2,3 (slopes 3.00, 6.00, 8.99). The committed one-pole gate predicts EXACTLY 3; 6 would mean two poles; anything not a multiple of 3 rules out the rational-pole form. Crucially THE EXPONENT IS PARAMETER-FREE EVEN THOUGH THE AMPLITUDE IS NOT: omega_c enters the amplitude but not the exponent, and that asymmetry is why this is worth measuring. Three mass powers follow from the same closed form: r_gate ~ M^0.3333, r_efe ~ M^0.5000, fixed-separation excess ~ M^-0.9935 (asymptotic; knee-contaminated to M^-0.857 by 30 kAU). FEASIBILITY IS NOW RESOLVED, NEGATIVELY (new in v2; v1 left it open and flagged it as possibly fatal). We pulled the catalogue. At v1's own recipe cuts (d < 200 pc, R_chance_align < 0.1, RUWE < 1.4 both components, MS-MS) the El-Badry, Rix & Heintz (2021, MNRAS 506, 2269) Gaia eDR3 catalogue holds only 436/270/155/60/24/3 pairs across the 30->236 kAU bins -- 364 clean pairs beyond 50 kAU, ~70 beyond 100. The shape test needs ~2000 per bin for 5 sigma separation of p = 3 from p = 0.5 (~400 gives only ~2.3 sigma). Relaxing the distance cut does not rescue it: proper-motion velocity error scales as (distance x pm error) while the requirement scales as sigma^2, and even at face value only 2 of 6 bins clear 2000. Ground-based astrometry cannot substitute -- the test needs sigma_pm <~ 0.02 mas/yr at 200 pc and Rubin/LSST delivers ~0.1-1.0 over ten years. GAIA DR4 IS THE ONLY ROUTE. PRE-REGISTERED, HASH-STAMPED, BEFORE THE DATA. Amendment 1 to the frozen Gaia DR4 pre-registration (2026-07-27, SHA-256 a309a502332b84ad521385b1c2031652849c9ce358c396f680f2308dd5ba1c13) records the frozen prediction p = 3; records gamma_v = 1.0004-1.0006 inside 2-30 kAU, so A NEWTONIAN DR4 RESULT IN THAT WINDOW CONFIRMS THIS BRANCH RATHER THAN REFUTING IT (the unamended pre-registration would have scored that as a kill); lists the five falsifiers; and states that DR4 gamma_v constrains the nu+EFE+gate prescription and NOT the value of a0 or Z. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. Not a test of a0 or Z: a confirmed s^3 rise establishes a frequency scale omega_c and a one-pole response. Z = 5.7888 and the conventional 2pi = 6.2832 differ by 7.87%, both sit inside the +/-16% empirical a0 box, and no arena here separates them; against interest, matching Chae (2024b)'s central gamma on this framework's own kernel needs a0 ~ 1.9x canonical, which at face value disfavours the Lambda-tied coefficient specifically. NOTHING about whether dark matter exists: a wide-binary result constrains the weak-field FORCE LAW, not the matter content, and gamma_v = 1 is Newton's prediction, shared by LambdaCDM, by this framework's own gated branch, and by modified-force-plus-particle hybrids. a0's value, Z, s = -1 and omega_c are POSTULATED, NOT DERIVED. CORRECTIONS CARRIED FROM V1, recorded rather than quietly fixed: the 200-vs-30 kAU excess ratio is 7x, not the >10x first stated; the fixed-separation mass scaling is asymptotic and knee-contaminated by 30 kAU; the operative sample requirement is the shape test's ~2000 pairs/bin, not the ~265 that excess-detection alone implies; and omega_c is now declared a free parameter rather than described as a constrained window. All numbers are printed by committed scripts, all exit 0, no hard-coded verdicts, both a0 footings and both omega_c edges throughout, at https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula
notes: VERSION 2. Supersedes v1 (2026-07-25) on four counts: (i) the DC/AC branch ambiguity v1 was explicitly conditional on is SETTLED from the framework's own action (Box_u u_mu = -Omega^2 u_mu identically), so the prediction no longer rests on a choice; (ii) the exponent is generalised -- an n-pole gate gives s^(3n), so the measured log-slope returns the pole count; (iii) the feasibility question v1 left open is answered NEGATIVELY from the actual catalogue (364 clean pairs beyond 50 kAU vs a ~2000/bin requirement), so the test waits for Gaia DR4; (iv) omega_c is now DECLARED A FREE PARAMETER rather than presented as a constrained window -- while the gate's EXISTENCE is shown to be forced by the kernel's own lack of high-frequency roll-off. Strict both-ways discipline: the exponent is parameter-free but the amplitude is not, and the paper says so; four v1 numbers are corrected in the open. Milgrom (1999) credited in the abstract and Section 1 for the kernel and identity, with priority for the a0-Lambda tie explicitly disclaimed.
